Team — forwarding Horizon’s request. TL;DR: potential new mid-enterprise logo, TCV ~ $320k ARR (first-year bill), they require Net-90 and quarterly invoices tied to their fiscal quarter.

Why this needs exec attention:
- Cashflow: Net-90 materially shifts cash timing for the ARR (impact for Q1 recognition).
- Precedent: granting quarterly invoicing + Net-90 could set an unwanted precedent for similar public-health customers.
- Time: Horizon asks for a contract/PO signature within two weeks to hit their budget window.

Customer ask (copied from their PO):
- Net-90 payment terms
- Quarterly invoices (one invoice per quarter for services)

Recommended options (ranked):
1) Approve Net-90 for 12 months as an exception, with a one-time setup fee of $10,000 and a 1.0% price uplift to offset DSO risk. Require signed PO referencing MSA and ACH/credit card on file for first invoice.
2) Counter with Net-60 standard terms and offer quarterly invoices only if they commit to a 50% upfront payment for first quarter.
3) Decline Net-90 — keep standard Net-30/Net-60 and escalate if we lose the deal.

Attachments: [Horizon_PO.pdf, contract_redlines.docx, approval_matrix.xlsx]

Requesting: Neha — finance impact & approval path; Rishi — legal review of redlines and proposed clause about late-payment interest and SLA holdbacks; Lauren — final sign-off threshold (is Net-90 + fee acceptable to keep the deal).

Quick finance read:
- Revenue recognition: Net-90 pushes cash collection outside of the initial service period; we can still recognize ARR under ASC 606 if we have sufficient enforceable contract terms and a signed PO, but it increases churn/credit risk exposure.
- DSO impact: Net-90 versus Net-30 on a $320k ARR deal means ~$240k of cash moved out of the quarter in which the service is delivered — material for our Qs.

Mitigations I’m comfortable with:
- One-time non-refundable setup fee of $10,000 charged at contract signing (immediate cash).
- 1.0% pricing uplift across the term OR 50% upfront for the first invoice. Prefer the uplift for operational simplicity.
- Require signed PO referencing the MSA + a primary AP contact.
- Perform a quick credit check (I’ll coordinate).

If legal signs the late-payment interest/SLA clause and credit check is decent, I will approve the exception to Net-90 under the above conditions. Please confirm the exact invoice numbering cadence Horizon expects so ERP can map quarterly invoices.

I’ve attached an approval_matrix.xlsx that shows thresholds and who needs to sign for this size.
